findings.title: Dancers cannot apply any follow-up voice edit — the new edit endpoint requests the nonexistent Claude model on both attempts and has no edit fallback
findings.observed: Add, remove, budget and delivery commands return applied=false after both model calls fail.

findings.title: Khmer-speaking dancers receive an English kit instead of Khmer instructions — the build fallback ignores the selected language
findings.observed: A lang=km build falling back returns English kit name, cue tips and filming tip.

findings.title: Dancers can lose their kit when sharing or ordering it — a failed database insert is swallowed even though the new share and checkout routes require that saved kit
findings.observed: A failed kit insert still returns 200; its share link and checkout subsequently return 404.

findings.title: First-time voice users can be recorded after releasing the mic — permission resolution starts the recorder after the release handler has already returned
findings.observed: Releasing while microphone permission is pending does not stop the newly started recording.

findings.title: Dancers still lose named songs not in the trend list — the changed fallback only recognizes exact cached trend titles and substitutes the generic song otherwise
findings.observed: A named song absent from trending sounds becomes 'Your trending track' in the fallback.

findings.title: Dancers still lose personalized AI-generated shot plans — both changed build attempts request the nonexistent Claude model before falling back
findings.observed: Both build attempts still request claude-sonnet-5-5, then serve the fixed fallback kit.

findings.title: Dancers still lose their requested crew and firework choices when generation fails — the changed fallback builds the same fixed plan
findings.observed: Fallback cues and filming tip remain fixed regardless of requested crew or firework.

findings.title: Dancers can still order a different kit than the one selected — checkout reads the live card prop while an in-flight build or voice edit can replace it
findings.observed: A build or voice edit finishing during checkout replaces the kit used by payment.

findings.title: Khmer-speaking dancers can receive a kit over their stated riel budget — the budget parser recognizes only English currency words and the fallback ignores Khmer budget text
findings.observed: A Khmer request for ៤០០០០ រៀល has no parsed budget; fallback costs $13, not $10.

findings.title: Dancers lose voice-set delivery details on reload or sharing — the edit returns delivery separately without storing it in the kit revision
findings.observed: GET /api/shot-kit/{id} omits delivery; reopening a shared edited kit loses spot and time.

findings.title: Dancers can get the item they removed put back in their kit — cue padding and budget swaps unconditionally choose catalog items without respecting the edit command
findings.observed: Removing confetti can refill or swap cues to item 6, Confetti Popper.

findings.title: Dancers can have unrecognized voice commands silently rewrite a kit — every parseable model response is stored as an applied revision without checking intent or changes
findings.observed: A parseable response to an unsupported command is stored with applied=true.

findings.title: Dancers can have an in-flight voice edit overwrite a newly built kit — the Build button remains enabled while editKit awaits its response
findings.observed: Build can complete during an edit; the later edit response replaces the new card.

findings.title: Shoppers without WebGL cannot reliably browse the Stand — the new card grid always mounts a Three.js Canvas with no capability check or error boundary
findings.observed: The Stand always constructs a WebGL Canvas and has no static-card error fallback.

findings.title: Dancers download a clip missing the visible phone-view overlays and DROP label — recording captures only the canvas instead of the composed preview frame
findings.observed: The saved clip captures only canvas pixels, omitting the phone overlay and DROP label.

findings.title: Dancers closing a recording preview can get an unwanted later download and active capture — Escape bypasses the disabled close button and no recorder or timer is cleaned up
findings.observed: Escape closes a recording preview but its 15.3-second timer and capture stream continue.

findings.title: Dancers can get stuck in a fake recording when capture fails — recorder creation and start run in an unguarded timer after the controls are disabled
findings.observed: A MediaRecorder or captureStream exception leaves recording=true and controls disabled.

findings.title: Khmer readers cannot translate an already-built or shared kit by switching language — the toggle changes UI labels but never translates the displayed kit data
findings.observed: Switching EN to Khmer after building leaves the existing kit name, tips and song in English.

findings.title: Khmer speakers can get mistranscribed when their interface is in English — transcription forces the UI language instead of detecting the language spoken
findings.observed: A Khmer clip without the language field is forced through Whisper with language=en.

findings.title: Dancers can still lose their selected drop firework — the changed planner substitutes a cheaper item when the budget is tight
findings.observed: An unaffordable drop line is still replaced with a cheaper catalog item.

findings.title: Dancers can still receive their largest firework away from the beat drop — the changed builder protects an existing drop cue without comparing it with other cues
findings.observed: An existing drop cue is kept even when a more expensive cue occurs elsewhere.

findings.title: Dancers can leave orphaned kit revisions after an edit reports failure — the endpoint inserts the kit before validating the model's changes field
findings.observed: Invalid changes data can throw after insert, leaving a saved revision while applied=false.

findings.title: Dancers can receive an over-budget kit after a riel voice edit — a positive model budget overrides the server's currency parser without validation
findings.observed: A model budget_usd of 40000 overrides the parsed 40,000 riel value of $10.

findings.title: Dancers can order a new kit to the previous kit's destination — building a replacement never clears the separate voice-delivery state
findings.observed: Building a second kit retains the previous voice-edited delivery spot and time.

findings.title: Dancers cannot undo a misheard voice edit or restore its share link — the previous kit is kept only for a temporary highlight and no revert action is rendered
findings.observed: No control restores changes.prev; the previous revision is discarded from UI state after 9s.

findings.title: Dancers cannot see exactly what a voice edit removed or changed in delivery or total — highlights only compare cart rows that still exist and new cue keys
findings.observed: Removed cart lines disappear and changed totals or delivery receive no field highlight.

findings.title: Keyboard users can activate hidden home controls while browsing the Stand — the replacement portal has no initial focus, focus trap or background inertness
findings.observed: Opening the Stand leaves keyboard focus on the underlying home-page controls.

findings.title: Dancers relying on spoken confirmation still do not hear a delivery status — neither translated utterance names any status step
findings.observed: Both English and Khmer utterances omit Packed, On the tuk-tuk and Arrived.

findings.title: Dancers can still receive reconstructed plans missing intended cues — the changed builder silently discards invalid cue entries instead of retrying the response
findings.observed: Invalid cue entries are still discarded rather than triggering an LLM retry.

findings.title: Dancers can still be told a catalog item produces the wrong effect — the changed builder trusts the model's effect text instead of the catalog
findings.observed: The cue's displayed effect still comes from the unchecked model text.

findings.title: Customers can still lose their order confirmation while checkout is pending — the changed dialog remains dismissible while the order POST continues
findings.observed: The checkout dialog can still be dismissed while the order POST is pending.

findings.title: Stand visitors now see endless loading placeholders after a catalog network failure — the changed fetch still silently ignores errors
findings.observed: A failed catalog fetch leaves six loading placeholders with no error or retry.

findings.title: Dancers on tall narrow phones can still see a stretched phone preview — the changed frame constrains width without reducing height
findings.observed: The 9:16 frame still clamps width independently of its fixed height.

findings.title: Keyboard users can still activate hidden kit controls behind the preview — the changed overlay has no focus management or dialog semantics
findings.observed: The fullscreen preview still has no focus trap or dialog semantics.

findings.title: Dancers still cannot pause the preview to inspect a cue — the changed timeline has no pause state or control
findings.observed: The changed preview still advances continuously with Replay but no Pause control.

findings.title: Dancers can think they copied a share link when nothing was copied — the fallback ignores execCommand's failure result and always shows success
findings.observed: If clipboard access fails and execCommand returns false, the app still says Link copied.

findings.title: Keyboard users still cannot record a voice request or follow-up edit — the changed mic handles pointer events only
findings.observed: The changed edit mic still handles only pointer events, not keyboard press and release.

findings.title: Phone users can still lose long song names or filming instructions — the changed kit card clips unbreakable text
findings.observed: Long unbroken song names or filming tips still sit inside an overflow-hidden card.

findings.title: Dancers can still fire fractional cues at the wrong moment — the changed card rounds seconds and marks nearby cues as the drop
findings.observed: A cue at 8.4 seconds still displays as 0:08 and may be marked as the drop.

findings.title: Dancers still see DROP stuck over the final preview frame — the changed overlay ties label expiry to a clock capped at 15 seconds
findings.observed: A drop at 14 or 15 seconds still leaves the DROP label on the final frame.

findings.title: Dancers can still see a mixed or incomplete preview when a kit changes — the changed card passes the live kit into a director with the old fired-cue state
findings.observed: A build or edit completing while preview is open replaces kit data without resetting fired cues.

findings.title: Dancers can still build a kit for their old request while a new recording transcribes — the changed mic does not share processing state with Build
findings.observed: Build remains enabled while the changed mic is transcribing a new recording.

findings.title: Dancers still get a fallback firework at the wrong time for a 15-second drop — the changed fallback uses the parser that clamps drops to 14
findings.observed: A requested drop at 15 seconds is still clamped to 14 in the changed fallback.

findings.title: Khmer readers must choose their language again on every visit — the selection is kept only in React state
findings.observed: Reloading after choosing Khmer resets the selected language to English.

findings.title: Stand shoppers must retype an item name to request it — cards expose only their particle-demo action
findings.observed: A Stand card tap only starts a demo and never adds its product to the request.

findings.title: Customers can see delivery progress move backwards after changing language — the language-dependent speech effect restarts the status timers
findings.observed: Switching language after Arrived schedules a return to On the tuk-tuk four seconds later.

findings.title: Khmer users encounter untranslated preview labels and shared-link errors — those strings bypass the translation dictionary
findings.observed: Khmer mode still exposes English Share, DROP, preview aria labels and link-error text.
